tests.name: power_on_selftest
tests.description: Boot the unit and enumerate devices on I2C, UART and CAN.

tests.name: battery_rest_check
tests.description: Read pack and per-cell voltages at rest.

tests.name: esc_telemetry
tests.description: Read ESC telemetry: sync errors, packet loss, back-EMF detection.

tests.name: compass_static
tests.description: Compare compass heading to the fixture reference with motors off.

tests.name: harness_continuity
tests.description: Measure per-bus continuity resistance and CAN termination.

tests.name: camera_selftest
tests.description: Run camera built-in self test and measure frame rate and CSI errors.

tests.name: imu_static
tests.description: Log 1000 IMU samples on the static fixture: gyro bias, accel noise, dropouts.

tests.name: motor_spin_test
tests.description: Spin all motors at 50 percent throttle: current, RPM, RPM jitter, temp.

tests.name: compass_motor_interference
tests.description: Sweep throttle 0-75 percent and log compass heading deviation.

tests.name: battery_load_test
tests.description: Apply a 20 A load and measure sag, cell imbalance, internal resistance.

steps.thought: I will run the power_on_selftest to quickly check communication across all major buses (I2C, UART, CAN) and catch any basic boot faults.
steps.observation: The power-on selftest failed because only 3 of 4 CAN nodes were enumerated, pointing to a potential CAN bus termination, wiring, or node fault.

hypotheses.rationale: Missing one CAN node during enumeration frequently points to a missing or disconnected CAN bus terminator.
A damaged CAN stub wire could also prevent one of the four nodes from enumerating correctly.

steps.thought: I will run the harness continuity test to check the CAN bus termination resistance and stub wiring integrity, which is the most direct way to distinguish between a missing terminator and a damaged stub wire.
steps.observation: The harness continuity test revealed a CAN termination resistance of 120.3 ohms, which is well above the normal range (54-66 ohms) expected with dual 120 ohm terminators, confirming a missing CAN bus terminator. This directly explains why only 3 of 4 CAN nodes enumerated successfully.

hypotheses.rationale: Measured CAN bus termination resistance of 120.3 ohms points directly to a missing or disconnected 120 ohm terminator, which also explains the failure to enumerate all 4 CAN nodes during boot.
Unlikely given the measured termination resistance is exactly near single-terminator level rather than an open circuit stub, but retained as a minor alternative.
